scope: Resolve RM306-TRANSACTION-CAPABILITY-LIFETIME and RM306-SPARSE-PAYLOAD-CANONICALIZATION in the private generated-host storage primitive, including view/retry/savepoint lifetime and suspended SQL continuation checks. Approval does not extend to unrelated target.rs code, compiler job declarations, worker scheduling or full ASYNC conformance.

corrections.assessment: Each outer attempt allocates a fresh private state only after the transaction opens. Its client and derived views share that state, while another outer transaction/retry gets a different state. Both adapters revoke active on every work exit before reset/COMMIT, with finally covering errors. Nested entry rejects inactive state; successful or rolled-back savepoints do not revoke the still-live outer token. Outbox enqueue requires a live token, and each execute checks again both before entering the wrapper and in the SQL invocation callback. The latter prevents a continuation delayed by an await/timeout-refresh from using a revoked handle.
corrections.independentEvidence: Exact emitted client wrappers, transaction method and view methods plus the unmodified production outbox include were evaluated against in-memory SQLite. Twenty-four stale enqueue/nested-entry calls were rejected across retained clients/views after commit, rollback, during an unrelated active transaction, and during/after retry replacement. A retired first attempt left no intent, the replacement got sequence 1, and a nested rollback followed by success also got sequence 1.
corrections.awaitRaceEvidence: For every enqueue SQL phase, the unmodified include was suspended in its asynchronous wrapper after the outer lifetime check, the token was revoked, then the wrapper resumed. All seven cases rejected delivery.transaction_required with zero additional SQL calls. This independently checks the callback-side lifetime guard after await, beyond the checked-in sequential stale-client regressions.
corrections.sufficiency: Sufficient for the two reported stale-handle paths and for preventing a new outbox SQL invocation after revocation. It does not cancel SQL already invoked while the token was live, confer authority on detached work, or prove a general driver/worker concurrency protocol. Generated callers must await their enqueue/nested operations within the source boundary.

corrections.assessment: Array normalization requires the ordinary Array prototype, exactly the length plus index own keys, and a data descriptor for every index. It reads descriptor.value rather than evaluating accessor elements. Sparse arrays, dense undefined elements, extra properties, accessor entries and subclasses therefore cannot alias valid explicit-null arrays. Valid dense [null] remains accepted and idempotent.
corrections.independentEvidence: The unmodified production include rejected all five unsupported array shapes before any SQL call. An accessor's getter was never evaluated. Explicit [null] persisted successfully; the root nontransactional read found it after token revocation. The checked-in generated-host test covers holes, undefined, extra properties, accessor entries, no intent/key writes, and explicit-null success; subclass rejection was independently probed here.

retainedStorageLimits: The immutable source identity, payload/version and per-key counter SQL is otherwise unchanged by these corrections. Prior schema/backend/collision and concurrent-source-revision limits in the original review remain applicable.

Tables are lazily created at transactional enqueue; root read before schema initialization is not an empty-queue guarantee. CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS does not attest an existing layout or supply schema migration/collision handling.

One configured adapter and the exact compiler-owned v1 schema are assumed. Missing adapters, incompatible tables, corruption, UUID collisions, sequence exhaustion, payload size/depth limits and restored-record validation are not newly approved.

The active token guards the outbox and nested transaction entry. It is not a general lifetime guard for every unrelated generated persistence method. No blanket persistence-capability security approval is given.

Already-invoked statements remain governed by the selected adapter transaction and existing deadline/commit rules; the token is not hard active-query interruption or a replacement for awaiting generated source operations.

Nested transactions check lifetime at entry; their already-started asynchronous savepoint work is not revoked or drained by this token. Detached/unawaited nested work and arbitrary concurrent host callback use are outside this scoped approval, just as already-invoked outbox SQL is. Future generated callers must keep all such operations awaited within the outer boundary.

Payload arrays now have the reviewed dense-data constraint. Future compiler bindings still need exact typed payload/version validation; this correction does not newly certify object accessors, proxies or arbitrary privileged host values as authored payloads.
wholeTaskAndFutureBindingLimits: Host-supplied job/source operation/entity/revision/key/version strings remain private host inputs. Future declarations must derive them from checked source operations and preserve policy/authority. No authored/public endpoint exists for this primitive today.
No generated job/event declarations, durable claim/fence, attempt history, dispatch checkpoint, worker/scheduler, cancellation/receipt transitions, retention or operator replay approval.
Same-job/key commit serialization is not worker dispatch FIFO or terminal/unknown key-release conformance. Cross-process and generated-job crash/ordering traces remain required.
RM-306 and the ASYNC 18-case catalog remain incomplete. Recorded live PostgreSQL and supported-gate passes do not close unimplemented compiler/worker/schema/full-task acceptance conditions.
